title: Cut non-inlined VARCHAR group-key overhead in the radix aggregate (measure per phase, fix the largest delta)
reasons: no visible template faster beyond its noise (best: q16 -1.3%; needs at least -5%)
summary:
I didn't redo Step 1's timers. An earlier session already measured the phases with temporary timers (see notes), so I went straight to the fix for the phase with the biggest gap.

That gap is caused by the "unpartitioned staging" path in GroupedAggregateHashTable::FindOrCreateGroups. The join feeds the aggregate chunks of about 300 rows, so each chunk adds at most 4 new groups per partition, and those groups get appended to the unpartitioned collection first. When the table is abandoned or repartitioned, that collection is repartitioned (UnpartitionedToPartitioned). For rows with a heap, which non-inlined VARCHAR keys have, that step copies the heap again and recomputes the string pointers. The fix is a one-line extra condition: only stage when `layout_ptr->AllConstant()`. Rows with a heap now go straight to the partitioned data, which is the normal path. The change is in src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp.

Earlier per-phase CPU measurements for this change: Abandon 37→2 ms, MaybeRepartition 97→56 ms, distinct-sink AddChunk 253→221 ms. That leaves almost no gap between VARCHAR and fixed-width keys.

Bench on q16 against the current best was very noisy: -15.8%, -8.1%, +1.6%, -5.9% over four runs, median about -7%. The baseline itself moved between 152 and 194 ms, so the machine was loaded. The build is OK and results match on all bench runs.

I also ran one spill check: memory_limit 100MB, 4 threads, 5M groups keyed on a long VARCHAR plus a LIST, with count and count(DISTINCT). The sums came out right.
notes:
This is the same fix an earlier session found (memory: varchar-agg-unpartitioned-staging). Its bench was just as noisy (-17% to +2%). The gain is real in per-phase CPU but small in wall time on a loaded machine.

Remaining q16 cost is mostly per-row work:
- main hash table sink fed by the distinct scan: ~180 ms CPU
- distinct sink AddChunk: ~220 ms CPU
- distinct finalize: ~120 ms CPU

Ideas for later:
- Compact the join output chunks (300-row chunks hurt every downstream vectorised stage).
- Avoid re-hashing and re-sinking from the distinct table into the main table when the distinct grouping matches the main group keys plus the distinct column.

Gotcha: wrapping q16 in count(*) lets the optimizer drop the DISTINCT aggregate; use max(cnt) instead.
